steps.text: Sprinkle a pinch of baking soda into a 64-ounce, heat-proof glass pitcher. Pour in boiling water and add tea bags. Cover and allow to steep for 15 minutes.
Remove tea bags and discard; stir in sugar until dissolved. Pour in cool water; refrigerate until cold, about 3 hours.
Enjoy over ice on a hot day!

raw_recipe.headline: Smooth Sweet Tea
raw_recipe.description: Sweet tea is a classic Southern drink made by steeping tea bags in a pitcher; sweeten with sugar and keep chilled for a refreshing drink on hot days!

review.reviewBody: I would give this recipe 100 stars if I could!!! I am in love with McDonalds sweet tea. I would go every morning after I dropped the kids off at school and buy 2 large teas with no ice. I would grab a drink here and there!! I would crave it if I didn't have any left!! Well sorry Mcdonalds!! You have met your match!! I double this recipe and make a gallon of sweet joy!! I love the baking soda trick. It really does keep the tea clear and not bitter. Thank you so much for this recipe!!!

As if this recipe needed ANOTHER 5 star rating, but I couldn't help myself. I agree with another reviewer that the baking soda DOES take the bitterness out of the recipe. I had stopped making iced tea for that very reason, and then I found this recipe. It's absolutely delicious. For those of you who see the baking soda in this recipe and frown in curiosity, turn that frown upside down. The baking soda makes it delicious (and is necessary in my opinion)! Now, I will say that I did not use quite as much cool water as the recipe calls for. I think I stopped at about 4 cups. But the strength of your tea is such a personal taste thing, so I would recommend that as you're adding the water, give it a good stir after the first few cups and taste it and see whatcha think. As for the sugar, I used exactly what the recipe called for (keep in mind I used less water) and it tasted perfect. Not too sweet, because I don't like sweet, sweet tea. This recipe can be tweaked to suit any taste. Thanks so much for sharing this wonderful recipe. It's absolutely delicious! Try it...once you do, you won't have it any other way!

Had a landscaping crew at the house on a HOT, humid day. I whipped up this tea and it got rave reviews from everyone. One of the guys grew up in Florida and said this was just like he remembered. So this is officially my sweet tea recipe.

Preparation notes: I used 1 teaspoon of loose leaf Lipton tea per bag required in the recipe. Add 2-3 cups of boiling water, tea, sugar, and baking soda into a metal Dutch oven so nothing shatters. Let tea steep 15 minutes. Fill measuring cup with ice, top off with cold water and mix with tea. Add however many cups of water are left. This “rapid chill” gets the tea colder faster. No need to chill for 3 hours in a fridge. Strain into pitcher and enjoy immediately!

Finally after making several different recipes I came upon this. After trying several different teas and experimenting I came up with the BEST tasting sweet tea ever. I used three of the Red Diamond (large) tea bags along with a regular size Earl Grey Bigelow black tea bag and put them in my Pyrex 8-cup shatterproof measuring cup with two cups bowling water and a pinch of baking soda. I let it steep for ten minutes, removed the tea bags put a cup of sugar in it...stirring really well, poured it into my ice tea pitcher followed by six cups of filtered water. The taste was perfect and so I chilled it in the fridge. Best tasting ice tea so far. Now,,, I just need to add a mint leaf, lemon wedges, ice and I am set for the warm summer months of Texas!!! Thanks to whoever posted this wonderful recipe. Awesome!!!

I don't have a large enough glass container so I boiled 4 cups water on the stove, added baking soda, mint sprigs and tea bags (2 peach, 5green tea) and steeped. Then I removed the mint and tea bags, added the sugar and 8 cups water, and placed in the refrigerator. Yumm!

I've been making this sweet tea since I was a child, my tea is almost exactly like this except I do not use the Baking soda , I boil the water in my little 16oz tea pot then turn the heat off and input my tea bags covering it with the lid for 30 min, put the sugar in the bottom of a 64 oz pitcher then pour in the still warm tea to desolve the sugar the fill the pitcher with water.... its ready to serve over ice ........ there is nothing on this earth more refreshing than a big ol tall glass of Texas sweet tea just like your Grandmother used to make.

Super easy recipe .... although I would prefer that an amount be specified instead of a "pinch" of baking soda (trust me too much is bad, not enough is worse). I have since found out that a "pinch" is an actual measurement that equals 1/8 teaspoon.

I lowered the sugar to 1/2 a cup as we all found it too sweet, we use Tetley tea bags so we lowered it to 5 bags and 17 minutes to steep.

Then once we add sugar, stir then I add 2.5 Tablespoons of lemon juice.

Absolutely love it - can be made with other flavoured teas as well. Blueberry white tea is AMAZING using this recipe.

I used 3/4 cup of Splenda instead of sugar and made 12 cups with 8 tea bags, steeped in 8 cups of boiling water, before adding the other 4 cups of cool water. I don’t like it too sweet and this was perfect for my taste. The baking side tip is really a game changer. Thanks for a terrific recipe!

Very good. I've made it with all kind of teas, black, green, flavored tea bags,.. They all made a delicious and refreshing iced tea. But I do cut the sugar down to half the amount.
Also I start the process of making this tea in my 4 cup Pyrex measuring cup ( this is after breaking 2 glasses pitchers last summer while making ice tea as directed here). The Pyrex can stand high heat and quick change in temperature. Then I fill my glass pitcher with cool water and pour the hot tea in it.
I added 6 tea bags to 4 cups of water, 1 cup of sugar after steeping and then an additional 6 cups of water to fill a 96 ounce glass pitcher.

Made a couple modifications because indont like super sweet tea. Put in about 1/3 cup sugar in my 2qt Takeya pitcher and filled half with boiling water. Added 4 Lipton tea bags and steeped for 5 mins. Filled the rest of pitcher up with ice and shook for 30 seconds.
It's our go-to sweet tea, and much more economical than store bought.

The recipe is fine. I add sugar and a handful of fresh mint while bringing the water to a boil and adding the tea bags. Steep for 5 minutes and remove tea bags and add the final delicious ingredients, juice from a lemon and an orange. Enjoy this recipe passed down to me from my mom. 💕
My family loved it, perfect for summer.
I did 1/2 amount-1 cup boiling water and 3 tea bags- 1 wild berry and 2 irish breakfast. Let steep for 15 min and Andes 1 tbls honey and 1/4 c sugar. THE BEST!
Great without sugar.

I've been making tea this way for a very long time. It usually goes first from the refreshments. That being said, I do have a few points to make. 1) The brand of tea used will make a difference in the taste. 2) If you use decaffeinated tea, by personal choice or health reasons, the finished product will usually be milder than regular tea. You may need to adjust the amount used. 3) The brand of sugar will also make a difference. There are some differences in sweetness between brands. You may need to make adjustments in amounts or try different brands until you find the one that suits your taste. The main takeaway I would say is this recipe is a good place to start. If you make adjustments is brands or amounts, don't forget to keep notes. You'll get to a final product you love!
I've been using this recipe for 15 yrs.
It was worth the time

I double-dog-dare anyone to make better sweet tea than this! Sweetness level: just right. Strength: just right. Clear: 100%. Bitterness: 0%. Difficulty: easy. Baking soda: a game changer! I sometimes add about 2/3 C fresh lemon juice. Try this if you like perfect sweet tea!
